title: Knowledge Graph Learning
summary: Chapter 5 focuses on how to leverage and traverse knowledge graphs to interpret domain-specific terminology and understand user search intent. The book divides this exploration into two main approaches: explicitly modeled knowledge graphs and semantic knowledge graphs (SKGs).

items.name: Arbitrary Relationship Extraction
items.description: Text is processed using natural language processing (NLP) libraries (such as spaCy) and dependency graphs to identify subjects, verbs, and objects, transforming unstructured sentences into queryable RDF triples (e.g., ['Data Scientists', 'write', 'code']).

items.name: Taxonomical Extraction
items.description: To reduce relationship noise, Hearst patterns are employed to automatically extract clean taxonomical hierarchies—such as hyponyms ("is a" relations) and hypernyms (broader categories).

sections.title: Semantic Knowledge Graphs (SKGs)
sections.description: An SKG is a dynamically materialized language model that does not require manual data modeling. Instead, it is built directly on top of a search engine's inverted index (mapping terms to documents) and forward index (mapping documents to terms, utilizing features like doc values). By traversing terms to documents and back to terms, the engine calculates edge weights (relatedness scores) based on statistical co-occurrences, allowing the system to discover semantic similarity in real time.

use_cases.name: Query Expansion
use_cases.description: Automatically expands query keywords with boosted, semantically related terms to improve search recall and precision (e.g., expanding advil to include ibuprofen or tylenol).

use_cases.name: Content-Based Recommendations
use_cases.description: Generates recommendations by extracting key terms from a document and scoring them against a topic via the SKG to build a highly relevant, context-aware query.

use_cases.name: Arbitrary Relationship Modeling
use_cases.description: Models specific, non-standard edge types (like "in love with") by combining starting nodes and relationship nodes in a search query.

title: Using Context to Learn Domain-Specific Language
summary: Chapter 6 shifts focus toward using behavioral user signals (such as search queries, clickstreams, and product interactions) alongside document content to dynamically learn domain-specific terminology, related concepts, and linguistic variations.

sections.title: Query Intent Classification
sections.description: Uses the SKG as a classifier to map incoming user queries to known, broad category nodes (e.g., classifying "docker" as devops or "passport" as travel) to enable intelligent query routing and category filtering.

sections.title: Query-Sense Disambiguation
sections.description: Resolves polysemy (words with multiple meanings) by applying a two-level SKG traversal. This process maps a query (like "chef" or "driver") first to its most likely category contexts and then extracts related terms specific to each distinct path (e.g., chef in a cooking context yields kitchen and ingredients, whereas in devops it yields puppet and ansible).

sections.title: Learning Related Phrases from User Signals

items.name: Query Log Mining
items.description: Groups sequential search queries from individual user sessions under the assumption that successive searches are refinements of the same intent. By tracking co-occurrences and calculating Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI₂), the system aggregates these patterns into a composite rank score that maps related searches while bypassing sparse-data noise.

items.name: Product Interactions
items.description: Overcomes the sparsity of user session data by grouping queries that lead to a click on the same target product. This aggregates collective user behavior to map closely related query variations.

items.name: Phrase Detection
items.description: Identifies multi-word entities by treating highly popular, raw user queries as single, unified entities (such as "hp touchpad" or "laser printer") rather than parsing them as independent boolean keywords.

items.name: Document-Based Spelling
items.description: Relies on index-level terms, which can be noisy and struggle to identify which suggestions represent actual user intent.

items.name: Signal-Based Spelling
items.description: Buckets query terms by search frequency—treating high-frequency terms as "corrections" and low-frequency terms as "misspellings". By pairing this popularity split with string edit distance heuristics customized by word length, the system generates clean, contextually accurate spelling corrections based on real user behavior.

title: Interpreting Query Intent Through Semantic Search
summary: Chapter 7 integrates the distinct query interpretation and domain-learning models discussed in earlier chapters into a unified, end-to-end semantic search pipeline.

key_phases.name: Parsing
key_phases.description: Deconstructs the raw query and extracts known entities, locations, or trigger words from an explicit knowledge graph rather than relying solely on naive keyword parsing.

key_phases.name: Enriching
key_phases.description: Evaluates the extracted entities and enriches them with context-aware classifications, related terminology, and semantic mappings from a Semantic Knowledge Graph (SKG).

key_phases.name: Transforming
key_phases.description: Utilizes adapters to convert the enriched query tree into a search engine-specific query DSL (like Apache Solr or OpenSearch).

key_phases.name: Searching
key_phases.description: Executes the transformed query against the search index and returns ranked results, using lexical and vector search backfills if precision filters yield too few results.

Programmatic query-rewriting rules bound to specific trigger words. For instance, a word like "top" triggers a function that boosts results based on user star ratings, while the word "near" transforms the subsequent entity into a geographic coordinate filter to constrain the search results to a specific physical radius.

title: Signals-Boosting Models
summary: Chapter 8 focuses on the mechanics of popularized relevance, which automatically optimizes rankings for your highest-volume queries by leveraging aggregated user feedback loops.

sections.title: Signal Aggregation & Normalization
sections.description: Captures query, click, and purchase signals and aggregates them. Normalization techniques (such as lowercasing user queries) are employed to group signals together and maximize their collective statistical significance.

sections.title: Spam Mitigation
sections.description: Combats malicious attempts to manipulate search rankings (signal spamming) by using user-based filtering algorithms that flag and ignore bot-like activity.

sections.title: Multi-Signal Blending
sections.description: Introduces weighting systems to combine diverse interaction types, scoring high-intent conversions (like purchases or add-to-carts) as significantly more important than standard clicks.

sections.title: Time Decays
sections.description: Implements half-life decay functions so that older signals gradually lose influence, allowing search results to dynamically adapt to seasonal shifts and trending products.

sections.title: Query-Time vs. Index-Time Boosting
sections.description: Evaluates the trade-offs between translating boosts on the fly (offering high flexibility but causing query bottlenecks) and storing boosts directly within document payloads at index-time (offering high scalability and consistent paging performance).

title: Personalized Search
summary: Chapter 9 explores shifting the search experience from global popularity to individual user preferences. It places personalized search on a continuum between traditional keyword search and collaborative recommendations.

sections.title: Collaborative Filtering
sections.description: Learns latent user and item features from behavior logs using Matrix Factorization (Alternating Least Squares or ALS) to predict user-specific ratings, which are then applied as personalized search boosts.

sections.title: Content-Based Personalization
sections.description: Builds a dynamic semantic user profile by mapping document interactions into a vector space. It implements K-Means clustering on text embeddings to categorize products and map queries to these topical clusters.

sections.title: Personalization Guardrails
sections.description: Solves the challenge of unrelated past interests skewing future searches. By applying categorical guardrails, the system prevents a user’s historical brand or style affinities in one category (e.g., electronic shavers) from bleeding into unrelated product categories (e.g., kitchen appliances).

title: Learning to Rank for Generalizable Search Relevance
summary: Chapter 10 introduces Learning to Rank (LTR), a methodology that uses machine learning to construct a generalized relevance model capable of ranking search results for completely unseen queries.

key_phases.name: Gather Judgments
key_phases.description: Compile a judgment list of query-document pairs, grading documents by their actual relevance.

key_phases.name: Feature Logging
key_phases.description: Configure the search engine to log numeric relevance scores (like title_bm25, overview_bm25, or release_year) representing query-document and document-only features.

key_phases.name: Machine Learning Transformation
key_phases.description: Normalize features. Reformulate the ranking task into a traditional machine learning classification problem using a pairwise algorithm (such as SVMrank), which maps the directional feature differences (deltas) between relevant and irrelevant document pairs.

key_phases.name: Model Training & Evaluation
key_phases.description: Train a classification model (like a Support Vector Machine), and evaluate its generalization success on a test query split.

key_phases.name: Deploy the Model
key_phases.description: Generate and upload the linear model weights directly to the search engine's model store.

key_phases.name: Rerank Search Results
key_phases.description: To minimize query latency in production, run a cheap, fast first-pass query (like BM25) to retrieve the top-N (e.g., 500) documents, and then execute the LTR model to rerank only that subset.

title: Automating Learning to Rank with Click Models
summary: Chapter 11 bridges LTR and behavioral signals by automating the creation of LTR judgment lists directly from user clickstreams. It details how to mathematically model and overcome human behavioral biases that corrupt raw click data.

key_phases.name: Position Bias
key_phases.description: Users are inherently biased to click items near the top of a results page, regardless of their actual relevance. The Simplified Dynamic Bayesian Network (SDBN) click model resolves this by tracking clicks with respect to whether a user actually examined a position (defining examination probabilistically based on the last click of a session).

key_phases.name: Confidence Bias (Low-Data Noise)
key_phases.description: Rare items that receive a single "lucky" click can mistakenly get a perfect relevance grade. To solve this, the chapter introduces the Beta Distribution as a tool to manage beliefs. By setting a baseline prior grade (e.g., 0.3) and a prior weight (confidence), the model gradually updates the relevance grade as more examines and clicks accumulate, keeping noisy, low-frequency data anchored to the prior.

title: Overcoming Ranking Bias Through Active Learning
summary: Chapter 12 tackles presentation bias—the critical feedback loop where users can only click on what is displayed, causing LTR models to continuously reinforce and overfit to existing search results.

sections.title: Active Learning
sections.description: Rather than exploiting only known relevant items, an active learning pipeline thoughtfully introduces strategic exploration to gather user feedback on unseen documents and expand training data coverage.

sections.title: Gaussian Process Regression (GPR)
sections.description: Uses a GPR model to analyze historical user signals, predict the relevance of candidate feature combinations, and calculate the uncertainty (standard deviation) of those predictions.

sections.title: Expected Improvement (EI)
sections.description: Applies an EI algorithm to balance the risk of showing poor results with the potential knowledge gained from exploration. It automatically selects and inserts high-uncertainty documents into live search results to gather unbiased feedback.

sections.title: Production Monitoring
sections.description: Evaluates LTR models through live A/B testing, tracking business outcomes (such as conversion rates) to validate offline relevance improvements.

title: Semantic Search with Dense Vectors
summary: Chapter 13 introduces dense vector search, leveraging the contextual representations of meaning (embeddings) generated by Transformer-based large language models.

sections.title: Transformers and SBERT
sections.description: Refreshes how Transformer encoders construct contextual vectors, and introduces Sentence-BERT (SBERT) to pool token vectors into high-quality, single-sentence representations.

sections.title: Key Implementations
sections.description: Walks through building natural language autocomplete pipelines (chunking nouns and verbs, generating embeddings, and querying an Approximate Nearest Neighbor or ANN index), and indexing document fields (such as titles) for direct semantic recall at query time.

items.name: Quantization
items.description: Explores scalar, binary, and product quantization (PQ) to compress high-dimensional vectors and dramatically reduce memory footprint and search times.

items.name: Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL)
items.description: Leverages embeddings trained to pack their most important semantic concepts into their earliest dimensions, allowing vector truncation to speed up initial matching while preserving recall.

items.name: Bi-encoders vs. Cross-encoders
items.description: Compares bi-encoders (which index queries and documents independently for fast ANN search) with cross-encoders (which joints queries and documents for highly precise, though computationally expensive, reranking).

title: Question Answering with a Fine-Tuned Large Language Model
summary: Chapter 14 dives into extractive question answering, using fine-tuned models to locate and extract the exact text spans that answer a user query.

sections.title: Retriever-Reader Pattern
sections.description: Combines a high-recall retriever (the search engine) to find relevant candidate documents with a high-precision reader (the fine-tuned LLM) that reads these documents and identifies the exact character offsets for the start and end of the answer span. A reranker then sorts the extracted answers based on their probability scores.

sections.title: Dataset Curation
sections.description: Outlines how to construct a question-answering dataset by building a silver set (automatically labeled guesses from a pretrained SQuAD2 model) and refining it into a highly trustworthy golden set through human-in-the-loop manual corrections.

sections.title: Fine-tuning & Evaluation
sections.description: Details how to split text contexts into tensors of equal length using sliding-window tokenization (accounting for overlap and padding) and fine-tune a model to minimize loss on holdout validation sets.

title: Foundation Models and Emerging Search Paradigms
summary: Chapter 15 explores the frontier of search in the age of generative AI, highlighting emerging paradigms where search engines and foundation models converge.

key_phases.name: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)
key_phases.description: Uses search engines as factual knowledge bases to retrieve up-to-date and accurate context, passing it to an LLM to generate grounded, hallucination-free responses.

key_phases.name: Generative Search Applications
key_phases.description: Demonstrates results summarization with citations and programmatically generating synthetic, domain-specific queries and relevance judgments to bootstrap other machine learning models.

key_phases.name: Multimodal Search
key_phases.description: Builds vector indexes that cross-modalize text and visual content, allowing text queries to find images, image queries to find related images, and hybrid queries combining both text and image modalities.

key_phases.name: Hybrid Search
key_phases.description: Combines the precision of lexical keyword search (BM25) with the conceptual recall of dense vector search. It details the Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) algorithm, which combines and reranks complementary result sets by summing the reciprocal of document positions.
